captions.text: Recap of chapter 04: two stars unpack a dictionary into named arguments.
A decorator takes a function and adds behavior.
A generator gives back one value at a time.
A context manager guarantees cleanup, even after an error.
Today's black box: how real projects are set up.
Let's open it.
A virtual environment is a private folder of packages for one project.
Activate it each time you open a terminal. Your prompt then shows .venv.
pip installs what's listed in requirements.txt.
These two packages also brought along the packages they need.
A test is code that checks your code.
pytest runs functions starting with test_. assert checks that something is true.
pytest.raises checks that an error really happens.
One command runs every test. Each dot is a test that passed.
When a test fails, pytest shows what it got. Here, 122 instead of 240.
The function added the numbers when it should have multiplied them.
HTTP is how programs talk over a network. Ollama is a small web server.
GET asks for data. A response has a status code and a body.
POST sends data. json= turns your dictionary into JSON for you.
Always set a timeout, so a stuck server can't hang your program.
Now run it. 200 means it worked.
404 means not found. It's still a response, so always check the status code.
Your turn. Complete the TODOs, including writing your own test.
You've finished when you see 5 passed. Then try the Part 0 checkpoint.
